newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Safras sees 74 pct rise in soybean exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Safras sees 74 pct rise in soybean exports.

text.p: Brazilian soybean exports should grow 74 percent to 6.3 million tonnes in the 1997/98 marketing year (February/January) from last year's 3.62 million tonnes, said independent consultants Safras e Mercado.
The projected sharp increase is due to the lifting of a state export tax last year which should favor soybean exports over sales overseas of soymeal and soyoil.
In its previous supply/demand forecast in December, Safras had forecast overseas soybean sales to reach 5.8 million tonnes.
Revenue from soycomplex sales should bring in $4.8 billion in 1997, exceeding last year's record $4.5 billion, Safras said.
Of the forecast 1997 receipts, $1.64 billion should come from soybean sales, $2.50 billion from soymeal exports and $650 million from soyoil sales.
Imports of soybeans are also likely to grow however to one million tonnes from a revised 1996/97 figure of 989,000 tonnes.
Soymeal imports are forecast to rise 34 percent to 150,000 tonnes from 112,000 last year while purchases of soyoil are expected to reach 200,000 tonnes, up 36 percent from 147,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
